author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canton unveiled a banner Thursday night honoring Michael Uliano, a hometown Army veteran who was killed in the September 11 attacks 25 years ago.

Uliano grew up in Canton and later worked for a financial firm in the North Tower of the World Trade Center. He was 42 when American Airlines Flight 11 struck the building on September 11, 2001, according to WHDH’s account of the town ceremony.

The banner was placed at a memorial already dedicated to Uliano. During the gathering, participants read the names of people killed in the attacks, lit candles and laid a wreath. The ceremony connected Canton’s local loss to the broader anniversary being marked across Massachusetts and the country.

The tribute gives residents a lasting, visible reminder of Uliano beyond the annual service. It also preserves the personal history of the attacks for younger residents who know September 11 only through family stories, school lessons and public memorials. Canton was among several Massachusetts communities holding observances on Thursday night and Friday.
dek: The town remembered the Army veteran and Canton native who was working in the World Trade Center’s North Tower.
headline: Canton unveils banner honoring September 11 victim Michael Uliano
